_why_this_fixture: POSITIVE, but for the CALENDAR rather than a live posting. This programme page states its own closure and reopening date in one quotable sentence, with NO YEAR given for '6 August'. This is the exact shape the 'never recall a date' rule exists for: a model asked cold 'when does CERN reopen' would confidently invent a year. Here the extractor's job is to surface the row as OUT-OF-STAGE (no current opening) while attaching the exact reopening quote as evidence, so calendar.py can decide the year from context (the fetch date) rather than from memory. This is not a job listing, so 'roles' stays empty by the strict per-posting schema; the reopening evidence is what feeds the calendar update, checked separately below.

programme_evidence.status_quote: This programme is now closed. We will reopen applications on 6 August. Please check back then for the updated vacancy announcement, or create a job alert to be notified when applications reopen.
